Measured on a copy of the live store (9,731 entries), tracemalloc peak during the call, each read in its own process, outputs saved as JSON from origin/main 3b80ff04452 (before) and from the change (after) and compared for equality. All 11 equal.
- search full (query 'memory', 253 rows): 348.9 -> 66.4 MB, equal
- search lean: 348.7 -> 66.4 MB, equal
- recent_session_logs (limit 5): 284.4 -> 10.8 MB, equal
- binding drift (audit_binding_drift): 328.7 -> 66.4 MB, equal (9 drift classes)
- validate (normalize_issues over _raw_tickets, 213 issues): 284.4 -> 12.6 MB, equal
- validate_state full report: 284.4 -> 12.3 MB, equal
- ticket_deps graph-cache miss (_compute_dep_graph on this ticket): 284.5 -> 44.4 MB, equal
- list --status=open full body: 284.4 -> 11.7 MB, equal (92)
- list --status=open lean (CLI shape): 64.2 -> 11.0 MB, equal
- list open + blocking_state=unblocked full body: 284.4 -> 47.9 MB, equal (69)
- list open + blocking_state=unblocked lean: 64.9 -> 46.4 MB, equal; the remainder is find_ready_tickets' lean pass, unchanged by design.
The remaining 66.4 MB in search and drift is the binding store: binding_jira_key_map alone peaks at 66.4 MB parsing the 22 MB bindings.json. That load predates this change; filed separately. The observation's 106.6 MB for the blocking_state list was not reproduced: the CLI-shaped lean read measured 64.9 MB here.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`reduce_all_tickets` (src/rebar/reducer/_api.py) applies `exclude_archived`, `exclude_deleted` and `exclude_session_logs` only after its loop finishes, and callers filter only after it returns, so every ticket that will be discarded is held in memory until then. Code reviews are 3,439 of 9,727 store directories. Measured on an isolated copy of the live store, 2026-10-29 (tracemalloc peak during the call, current caches):

| Read | Peak now | Peak with an in-loop filter and field trim | Output compared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` (`reads.py` `search_state`, full state, 141 matches) | 348.8 MB | 24.6 MB | identical (141 = 141) |
| `recent_session_logs` (full state, keeps 5) | 284.3 MB | 10.8 MB | identical |
| `bridge_fsck` binding-drift step (uses ticket_id, status, archived) | 328.6 MB | 69.5 MB (66.3 MB of it is binding/Jira data) | drift counts identical |
| `validate` (full-body list) | 284.3 MB | 49.3 MB | report identical |
| `ticket_deps` on a graph-cache miss | 284.9 MB | 64.2 MB | not compared |
| `list_tickets --status=open` | 64.1 MB | 11.0 MB | ids identical |
| `list_tickets` with `blocking_state` (holds pass 1 during `find_ready_tickets`) | 106.6 MB | not prototyped | — |

I confirmed the `search_state` and `recent_session_logs_state` calls and the post-loop filters by reading the code.

Re-measured on a fresh copy, 2026-10-29, before any change (peaks reproduce): search full 348.9 MB, recent_session_logs 284.4 MB, binding drift 328.7 MB, validate 284.4 MB, deps cache miss 284.5 MB.

Findings from reading the code that change the plan:
- The binding-drift step lives in `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py` (not `_commands/`). It reduces with no exclusions and reports every non-bound local ticket, including session logs and code reviews, as `unbound_local`, so it can only be trimmed (to `ticket_id`/`id`/`status`/`archived`; `reconciler/classify.local_state` reads only `archived` and `status`), not filtered.
- About 18 test modules replace `reduce_all_tickets` with stubs that ignore keyword arguments. Callers therefore keep their existing post-loop filters (they are pure predicates, so applying them a second time is a no-op on real data); the in-loop predicate only pre-narrows.
- `list_states` counts children over the reduced set before narrowing filters, so it can pre-filter in the loop only when neither `min_children` nor `with_children_count` is requested; otherwise it keeps the current path.
- Search matching happens in `search_states` (src/rebar/reducer/search.py); the in-loop matcher must be the same code, so it is split into a compiled per-ticket predicate that `search_states` also uses. Jira keys must be attached before matching because the haystack includes `jira_key`.

## Plan
1. Give `reduce_all_tickets` two optional keyword arguments: `keep` (a per-ticket predicate, applied after the existing exclusions) and `keep_fields` (a whitelist projection, the counterpart of `omit_fields`). Apply `exclude_archived`, `exclude_deleted` and `exclude_session_logs` inside the loop, so a discarded ticket is never appended. Error dicts keep their current treatment.
2. Move each caller onto it, keeping its post-loop filtering:
   - `search_state`: attach the Jira key and run the compiled search predicate inside the loop.
   - `recent_session_logs_state`: keep only session logs, project to `ticket_id`/`created_at`, sort, then re-reduce the top N in full.
   - `audit_binding_drift` (`_load_local_by_id`): project to `ticket_id`/`id`/`status`/`archived`.
   - `validate` (`_raw_tickets`): keeps reading through `reads.list_states` (its docstring pins list_states as the data source). `list_states` gains a keyword-only `keep` predicate that is ANDed into its in-loop pre-filter; every list_states transform after the loop (`apply_ticket_filters`, `public_state`, `lean_projection`, sort) is unchanged. `_raw_tickets` passes a predicate that drops `closed`/`error`/`fsck_needed`, the statuses `normalize_issues` discards anyway, so validate's issues and report are unchanged. No other list_states caller passes `keep`, so their output is unchanged.
   - `graph/_loader.load_indexed_states` (used by `ticket_deps` on a cache miss): drop unusable statuses in the loop and omit the body/signature fields the graph code never reads (it reads only ticket_id, status, deps, parent_id, archived, ticket_type). The field tuple moves into `graph/_loader.py` as `GRAPH_OMITTED_FIELDS`, with the same 6 names as today's `_READY_OMITTED_FIELDS`; `graph/_ready.py` already imports `_loader`, so it keeps its module-level `_READY_OMITTED_FIELDS` name (tests monkeypatch it) bound to that tuple, adding no new import and no cycle.
   - `list_states`: pre-filter in the loop with the same `apply_ticket_filters` call (plus any caller `keep`) when neither `min_children` nor `with_children_count` is requested; otherwise reduce as today. `find_ready_tickets` (the `blocking_state` pass) is not changed, so that row's saving comes only from the list rows.
3. Tests first (written before the change, seen failing): for each caller, a test that compares output with the old path on a fixture store containing archived, deleted, session_log and code_review tickets; a test that `reduce_all_tickets` never retains an excluded or `keep`-rejected ticket (by spying on the list it builds); and a test that each caller's projection or predicate is applied.
4. Measure each read's tracemalloc peak and compare outputs before and after on a copy of the live store, and record them on this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
Scope: the 7 reads in the table (search full and lean, recent_session_logs, binding drift, validate, ticket_deps cache miss, list_tickets --status=open, list_tickets with blocking_state).
- [ ] On the fixture store (archived, deleted, status-only deleted, session_log, code_review and corrupt tickets), each of the 7 reads returns output equal to the same read with the new `keep`/`keep_fields` arguments stripped; verified by tests/unit/test_reduce_all_in_loop_filters.py.
- [ ] On a copy of the live store, each of the 7 reads returns output equal (JSON comparison) to the output saved from origin/main before the change; recorded in a ticket comment.
- [ ] Each of the 7 reads' tracemalloc peak on that copy, before and after, is recorded in a ticket comment.
- [ ] A ticket dropped by `exclude_archived`, `exclude_deleted`, `exclude_session_logs` or `keep` is unreachable before `reduce_all_tickets` reduces the next directory; verified by a weak-reference test in the same module that fails on origin/main.

## File impact (expected)
- src/rebar/reducer/_api.py
- src/rebar/reducer/search.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py
- src/rebar/graph/_loader.py
- src/rebar/graph/_ready.py
- src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py
- tests/unit/test_reduce_all_in_loop_filters.py
